# Rikiki

> Rikiki is a tiny (~43 KB gzip) Lit Web Components framework for technical
> presentations and product carousels. A deck is plain HTML: load a theme
> stylesheet, then the component bundle, then write a `<deck-root>` wrapping
> `deck-*` slide elements. No build step to author or run a deck.

This reference documents rikiki v0.8.0.

The framework is opinionated:

- Web standards only (Custom Elements, Shadow DOM, ES Modules, CSS Custom Properties).
- Zero-build for deck authors. Consumers never touch a bundler.
- Three-layer design tokens (`--rik-palette-*` private, `--rik-*` semantic, `--deck-<tag>-*` per-component).
- Plugins are opt-in and lazy-loaded (transitions, presenter window, Shiki, click-stages).
- The same `<deck-root>` engine drives slides AND swipe-able carousels via `autoplay` / `loop` / `swipe`.

## Reference

- [Working guide](docs/llms/rikiki-workflow.md): the short path from a brief to a
  file someone can present · seven steps, an editorial contract, nine
  compositions by intent with checked HTML, and the order to try fixes in. Start
  here; it says when to open the reference.
- [Full LLM reference](docs/llms/rikiki-reference.md) (served at `/rikiki/docs/llms/rikiki-reference.md`): the single source of truth · every tag, attribute, slot, design token, plugin, and recipe in one file. Read this first.
- [README](README.md): human overview, common patterns, theming notes.
- `npx rikiki init <name>.html`: writes a starter deck plus the runtime it loads, next to it. Nothing to copy by hand.

## Components

Authoring tags fall into four buckets (see the reference for the exhaustive attribute/slot tables):

- **Layouts (slide-level, direct children of `<deck-root>`)**: `<deck-cover>` · `<deck-section>` · `<deck-feature>` · `<deck-split>` · `<deck-feature-cards>` · `<deck-photo>` · `<deck-takeaway>` · `<deck-bento>`
- **Molecules (composed containers)**: `<deck-callout>` · `<deck-card>` · `<deck-md>` · `<deck-mermaid>` · `<deck-stat>` · `<deck-metric-list>` / `<deck-metric>` · `<deck-tier-list>` / `<deck-tier>` / `<deck-tier-arrow>` · `<deck-step-list>` / `<deck-step>` · `<deck-shortcut-list>` / `<deck-shortcut>` / `<deck-kbd>` · `<deck-stack>` · `<deck-grid>` · `<deck-point>` / `<deck-cell>` / `<deck-fit>` / `<deck-csv>` (the bento family · reach for `<deck-point>` when a bento item holds words, and `<deck-cell>` when it holds something measured such as fit-to-cell text, a diagram or an image)
- **Atoms (primitives)**: `<deck-badge>` · `<deck-kicker>` · `<deck-punch>` · `<deck-code>`
- **Runtime (authoring touchpoints)**: `<deck-root>` (navigation host) · `<deck-notes>` (speaker notes, read by the presenter window)

## Illustrations · choose before drawing

A slide's picture is written as data or as an intent, never as a coordinate.
Pick from what the picture says:

- **A scene** (`<deck-scene-cards|steps|flow|bars|matrix|ranges|lanes|units>` filled with `<deck-scene-item>`, composed with `<deck-scene>`): things of the same rank, steps in order, inputs into a hub, a few bars, a status matrix, durations on a scale, lanes cut by a gate, a crowd one cell per person. Each is an opt-in module (`dist/deck-scene-*.js`). The skill `rikiki-scenes` picks the shape; `npx rikiki scene plan <brief.json>` lists the candidates and `npx rikiki scene compile <brief.json> --candidate <id>` writes the slide.
- **A diagram** (`<deck-diagram>`): something demonstrated · a cause, a barrier, a bottleneck, a stock, a loop, a threshold, a trade-off, a drift, parts of a whole; a picture that changes on a click; a story played on entry; charts (`dg-pie`, `dg-columns`, `dg-waterfall`, `dg-curve`). Start from `npx rikiki intent "<sentence>"` or `npx rikiki recipe "<sentence>"` and read the skill `rikiki-illustrate`.
- **A hand-drawn SVG**: only when no scene or diagram says it. `rikiki check` measures its text and its frame like the others.

`rikiki check` proves each one: a scene that would draw silently (`SCENE_*`), a diagram that does not demonstrate its intent (`INT_*`), an illustration off-centre, crowded or too like the one before (`ILL_*`).

## Plugins (opt-in, lazy)

- **Transitions**: `transition="slide|slide-up|slide-down|slide-right|fade|zoom|flip"` on `<deck-root>` (per-slide `data-transition`).
- **Presenter window**: press `P` · mirrors current + next slide, timer, and `<deck-notes>`. With a second screen it sends the slides fullscreen to the projector and keeps the presenter view on the speaker's screen; previews are 16:9; the projected deck auto-hides its chrome while it's open.
- **Shiki highlighting**: the built-in `deck-code` highlighter knows js/ts/json/html/xml/svg/css/scss/less. The optional offline Shiki runtime provides TextMate highlighting for ts/typescript, js/javascript, html, css and json with the bundled `one-dark-pro` theme: `import { installShiki } from './dist/shiki.js'` then `await installShiki({ theme: 'one-dark-pro', langs })`. List only the supported languages the deck uses.
- **Click-stages**: `import { installClickStages } from './dist/click-stages.js'` then `installClickStages()` · per-element `data-click` / `data-anim` / `data-morph` reveals.
- **Slide zoom**: Ctrl/⌘+wheel / pinch / `+`/`-`/`0` magnify a slide (fixed canvas, on by default, pan by drag/wheel); `no-zoom` on `<deck-root>` opts out.
- **Writing a plugin**: `deckRoot.use(plugin)` with a `DeckPlugin` (`steps` / `applyStep` / `navigate` / `setup` hooks); `setDeckCodeHighlighter(fn)` overrides `<deck-code>` highlighting. Both re-exported from `dist/index.js`. `installShiki` / `installClickStages` are back-compat shims.
- **Livereload (authoring only)**: append `?live` to the deck URL.

## The CLI · what a consumer runs

Every command below works from an install, with no clone and no build step.

- `npx rikiki init <name>.html` · an editable source deck, plus the runtime
  copied into `./rikiki/` beside it. Serve that folder over HTTP · ES modules do
  not load from `file://`. Needs nothing but Node.
- `npx rikiki bundle <deck>.html [out.html]` · folds theme, runtime and images
  into one self-contained file, curated to the components the deck uses. Needs
  the optional peer `rolldown`.
- `npx rikiki render <deck>.html [--out dir] [--slides a,b] [--steps] [--baseline dir]` · one PNG
  per slide, a gallery and a `manifest.json` tying each picture to the slide it
  came from. This is how an agent sees a deck. `--baseline <dir>` compares each
  fresh picture to the same-named one of an earlier render and ranks the slides
  by how much moved. Needs the optional peer `playwright`.
- `npx rikiki check <deck>.html [--json] [--steps] [--slides 4,6-9] [--diversity]` · measures the deck in a browser and
  reports what is wrong: a runtime that never loaded, a missing file, a
  misspelled `deck-*` element, content clipped by the slide, text too small for
  a room, content painting outside its box or over a sibling, graph nodes
  overlapping each other. `--json` writes a versioned report to stdout and
  nothing else; `--steps` measures every revealed state of a slide instead of
  its opening one; it also says how alike the illustrations are to each other
  (`diversity`, `ILL_REPEATED_LOOK`, a motif that moves on excepted), checks
  the motifs a deck declares (`pair`, `zoom-from`, `acts`: `ILL_PAIR_*`,
  `ILL_ZOOM_FROM_TARGET`, `ILL_ACT_DRIFT`), and `--diversity` adds every distance.
  Exit 0 clean, 1 defects found, 2 could not look. A `check` section in
  `rikiki.config.json`, or `--checks`, `--severity`, `--warnings-as-errors`,
  `--limit`, drops or takes back rules, sets severities and moves thresholds
  (`--list-checks` says what a deck can meet). Needs `playwright`.
- `npx rikiki scene plan|compile|budgets` · turns a JSON brief into a slide made
  of a scene (see Illustrations). `plan` and `budgets` read no model; `plan
  --measure` also draws each candidate in a browser.
- `npx rikiki intent "<sentence>"` · prints the skeleton of the diagram intent
  closest to a sentence, with its roles and the mistakes `check` rejects;
  `npx rikiki recipe "<sentence>"` prints one of twelve graphic models told as a
  story, to fill from a brief (`--fill`). No model is called.
- `npx rikiki export <deck>.html [--output deck.pdf]` · one PDF page per slide.
  Needs the optional peer `playwright`.
- `npx rikiki skills` · installs the five agent skills (`rikiki-deck`, `rikiki-theme`, `rikiki-debug`, `rikiki-illustrate`, `rikiki-scenes`) into `.claude/skills/`.

A missing optional peer is reported with the command that installs it.
